Verified-as-of: 2483bd123e70164c921d4228ad18621132ceb38f

## Current State

The Context line cites commit `4c6e76733` as the deletion of the design doc that reasoned through this decision. `git cat-file -t 4c6e76733` returns "Not a valid object name", and `git rev-list --all | grep -i '^4c6e'` finds no match anywhere in this non-shallow repository's full history (verified via `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` -> false). The commit the ADR itself was authored in (`ec589b3dc`) does not delete any design doc either, so the deletion happened on a now-unreachable commit — most likely a worktree branch commit pruned after its PR merged, per this project's own worktree-cleanup convention. A reader or agent trying to inspect the original reasoning via this citation hits a dead reference with no indication of why.

## Deliverables

**Current:**
```
the design doc that reasoned this through was deleted at decomposition (`4c6e76733`), so the trade-off is recorded here
```

**Proposed:**
```
the design doc that reasoned this through was deleted at decomposition; the deleting commit is no longer resolvable in `main`'s history (consistent with a worktree branch pruned after merge), so the trade-off is recorded here instead
```

## Acceptance Criteria

Replace the unresolvable commit-hash citation in the Context line's design-doc-deletion clause with an honest note that the specific commit is no longer resolvable in `main`'s history (consistent with a worktree branch pruned after merge), so a reader following the citation isn't led to a dead end with no explanation.

groups.title: One injectable ghAvailable() helper for the six near-verbatim gh --version probes in plugin/bin
groups.body:
Defer-reason: genuinely-larger
Origin: reflect hindsight from #1988 (spec-1988/staged/reflect-1.md), re-routed by the batch reflect at the /flow #1988-#1997 consolidated close (parent run 2026-09-06T110420)

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/compose-context/resolve-conditions.js`'s `transport` probe (`execFileSync('gh', ['--version'], …)` in a try/catch) is the sixth near-verbatim copy of the `gh`-availability check in `plugin/bin` — `release-claim.js`, `lib/feedback/file-feedback.js`, `link-records.js`, `materialize.js`, and `lib/repo-resolve.js` each carry their own, with drifting option objects (`stdio: 'ignore'` vs `stdio: 'pipe'` + `timeout`). None share a helper, so a rule applied to one (a timeout bound, an env override for sandboxes) silently misses the rest — the drift shape `gh-api-module-pattern`'s "sibling default runners" bullet records for git/gh runner pairs. `grep -rn "'--version'" plugin/bin` lists the six sites. Raised by #1988's whole-branch review and its Task 2 reviewer independently; staged at #1988's hindsight reflect as a convention finding whose resolution is a follow-up record, which the consolidated console cannot file without this header.

## Deliverables

- One `ghAvailable(deps)` helper — injectable runner, one bounded options object (`stdio: 'ignore'`, a timeout) — in `plugin/bin/lib/repo-resolve.js` or a new `plugin/bin/lib/gh-available.js`.
- Migrate the six call sites to it; delete the local copies.
- A fake-runner test pinning the helper's shape (available / absent / throwing runner), and a grep-backed test that `'--version'` appears in `plugin/bin` only inside the helper.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `grep -rn "'--version'" plugin/bin` returns exactly one production site.
- Every migrated CLI's existing tests stay green with the helper injected.
- `npm test` green apart from the tracked baseline (#1900).


_Filed from the /flow #1988-#1997 consolidated Review Console (run 2026-09-06T110420, PR #1998); staged proposal: staged/record-proposal-4.md._

groups.title: friction-events.js returns every event type — filter to the Friction lens vocabulary its contract states
groups.body:
Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff
Origin: reflect full (batch) from /flow #1988-#1997 consolidated close (parent run 2026-09-06T110420)

## Current State

`reflect/full-mode.md`'s Friction lens says `bin/friction-events.js --run "$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR"` returns this run's events "filtered to: `wd-deny`, `gate-denial` and `bookkeeping-stamp-deny` …, `contract-violation` …, and `ask-user-question`". The CLI's `readEvents` (`bin/friction-events.js`) drops only test-tagged `gate-denial` rows (#1337) and fallback-attributed rows (#1402) and passes every other `type` through: on the #1988–#1997 parent run it returned 152 events — 101 `commit`/`push` bookkeeping rows, 3 `pre-compact`, a `session-end`, and a `skill_invoked`, alongside the 46 `contract-violation` rows the lens actually reads. Every lens run has to re-implement the type filter the contract says the tool performs, and a lens that trusts the contract reads a commit as friction.

## Deliverables

- Filter in `readEvents` (or in `run` before output) to the five types listed between `<!-- friction-lens-vocab:begin -->` and `<!-- friction-lens-vocab:end -->` in `reflect/full-mode.md` — one shared constant, so `tests/reflect-friction-lens-vocab.test.js` can pin the CLI's list against the same block it already pins the doc against.
- Keep the Membership rule's exclusions (`wd-foreign-session`, `wd-foreign-teardown`, `wd-ambiguous`, `wd-push-mismatch`) out by construction — they are not in the five.
- A fixture test: an `events.jsonl` mixing `commit`, `pre-compact`, `session-end`, and the five friction types yields only the five.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `node bin/friction-events.js --run {dir}` on a run dir whose `events.jsonl` holds only `commit` rows prints `[]`.
- The vocab test fails if the CLI's type list and the doc block ever diverge.
- `npm test` green apart from the tracked baseline (#1900).


_Filed from the /flow #1988-#1997 consolidated Review Console (run 2026-09-06T110420, PR #1998); staged proposal: staged/record-proposal-3.md._

groups.title: plan-audit: Check C needs a "Step 2 present but unparseable" diagnostic signal
groups.body:
Title: plan-audit: Check C needs a "Step 2 present but unparseable" diagnostic signal
Type: task
Labels: risk:low, size:small
Defer-reason: tangential

# Ledger item 18 (from #903 review)

**Origin:** ledger resolve gate, spec #903 review
**Defer-reason:** tangential

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/parser.js`'s `parseStep2` returns `null` both when a task genuinely
has no TDD Step 2 and when it has a Step 2 whose wording/Run: format didn't match the parser's
patterns. `checks.js`'s `checkC` silently `continue`s either way with zero diagnostic output.
#903's review fix broadened the wording match to also accept "verify they fail" but deliberately
did not chase the further "confirm FAIL" + fenced-code-block-Run: drift observed in a real,
current plan (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-26-sweep-residue-needs-decision-marker.md`) — that
is a moving target for regex matching, and the durable fix is structural.

## Deliverables

- `parseStep2` (or a sibling function) reports a distinct "Step 2 present but unparseable" signal
  instead of collapsing into the same `null` as "no Step 2 at all".
- `checkC` surfaces that signal as a warning (not a hard failure) in its JSON envelope, naming the
  task and its raw Step 2 text so a human can judge whether the plan needs updating to the
  canonical template or the parser needs to learn a legitimately new shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A task with a Step 2 header matching no known wording variant, but bearing `- [ ]`/`- [x]`
   checkbox syntax, produces a distinct signal (not silently indistinguishable from "no Step 2").
2. `plan-audit.js`'s output surfaces this signal without failing the exit code on its own.
3. Regression test against the real `2026-08-26-sweep-residue-needs-decision-marker.md` plan
   shape (fenced-code-block Run:, "confirm FAIL" wording) demonstrating the new signal fires.

_Filed by `ledger resolve gate` via specShapedBody._

groups.title: Confirm RemoteTrigger update persists notifications, then close #68's guided-creation path
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

Refs #68. `skills/routine/create-and-update.md` now sets `notifications` unconditionally on the direct-create path (Step 6 body template), documents the field, and adds a Step 7 preview line stating a routine emails on every firing — all implemented and pinned by `tests/routine-notifications.test.js`. Step 8's guided-creation branch was also extended with a follow-up `RemoteTrigger {action: "update", trigger_id, body: {notifications: {...}}}` call, but its correctness for the `notifications` field specifically is unconfirmed: Task 0's empirical premise-check (does `RemoteTrigger update` actually persist `notifications` the same way `create` was already confirmed live) requires the `RemoteTrigger` tool, which was unavailable in both the original build session and this ledger-resolution session (`ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` returns no match in either).

**Shaping-time fact-check (2026-08-23):** the `RemoteTrigger` tool, previously unavailable in both prior sessions, is now available in this session (`ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` resolves it) — the same finding as sibling record #1302, filed from the same ledger-resolution pass. This shaping session did **not** attempt Task 0's actual premise-check: creating a throwaway routine via `RemoteTrigger` and confirming `notifications` persists is a real external-service mutation with no delete API to clean it up afterward (per the record's own Deliverables), which is build-time work requiring the build session's own judgment and authorization, not something to run speculatively during shaping. The build session should re-verify `RemoteTrigger` availability in its own environment before assuming this blocker is fully resolved — tool availability may be session-type-dependent (interactive vs. cloud/routine).

## Deliverables

- Re-verify `RemoteTrigger` availability via `ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` in the build session's own environment.
- Run Task 0's premise-check: create a disabled, cron-less throwaway routine, call `RemoteTrigger {action: "update", trigger_id, body: {notifications: {...}}}` on it, `get` it back to confirm the value stuck, then remove the throwaway by hand at claude.ai/code/routines (no delete API exists).
- If confirmed: mark #68 AC2/AC3 met — the guided-path follow-up call in `create-and-update.md` Step 8 is already implemented and needs no further code change.
- If NOT confirmed: redesign the guided-path follow-up around whatever mechanism the probe finds actually works, and update `create-and-update.md` Step 8 accordingly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Task 0's premise-check result (confirmed / not confirmed) is recorded in this record's resolution.
- `RemoteTrigger {action: "get"}` against a just-created routine (guided path) confirms it carries the same `notifications` value as the direct-create path — this is #68's own AC2.
- If Task 0 found the `update` mechanism does not work as assumed, `create-and-update.md` Step 8 is corrected and `tests/routine-notifications.test.js` (or a new test) pins the corrected behavior.

## Technical Approach

Re-confirm `RemoteTrigger` availability first (tool access may differ from this shaping session's environment). With the tool available, create a disabled, cron-less throwaway routine via the guided-creation path, call `RemoteTrigger {action: "update", trigger_id, body: {notifications: {...}}}`, then `RemoteTrigger {action: "get"}` to confirm the value persisted — matching the same confirmation already done for the direct-create path. Clean up the throwaway routine manually at claude.ai/code/routines afterward (no delete API exists — do not leave it dangling). Branch on the result exactly as the Deliverables state: no further code change if confirmed; a Step 8 redesign plus a pinning test if not.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/routine/create-and-update.md` — Step 8's guided-creation follow-up call, the thing being verified (and, conditionally, corrected)
- `tests/routine-notifications.test.js` — existing pins for the direct-create path; extend if Step 8 needs correction

## Gotchas

- The throwaway-routine creation is a real external-service mutation with no automated cleanup (no delete API) — this is exactly the kind of action that needs the build session's own explicit judgment, not something to attempt speculatively or headlessly without care.
- Tool availability was confirmed only in this shaping session, not the build session that will actually run the premise-check — re-verify via `ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` first; it may be environment-dependent (interactive vs. cloud/routine).
- Do not forget the manual cleanup step — a stray throwaway routine left in the account is a small but avoidable leftover.

## Original request

groups.title: Live-verify create_webhook_trigger request/response shape (#1302 follow-up, 4th recurrence)
groups.body:
Origin: ledger resolve gate

Defer-reason: blocked-dependency

## Current State

Record #1302 built the WEBHOOK-TRIGGER mode (`plugin/skills/routine/webhook-trigger.md`), the `webhook_triggers` schema field, the filter grammar, and both preconditions -- all documented from `create_webhook_trigger`'s own tool description, since `RemoteTrigger` was confirmed unavailable via `ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` in that build session. This is the 4th consecutive session (2026-08-23 x2, 2026-08-26, 2026-09-05) to confirm the same unavailability. AC2 ("verified against a real (or explicitly documented dry-run) call") remains unmet: the request/response shape has never actually been confirmed against a live `create_webhook_trigger` call.

A prior follow-up for this same gap, #1485, was filed and closed on 2026-08-31 -- but the closing commit (`e0d4aded`, "[fast-lane] Dispatch-queue, worktree-guard, reconcile, and process-hygiene fixes (19 records)") bundled 19 unrelated record numbers via `Fixes #N` and contains no work touching `webhook-trigger.md`, `RemoteTrigger`, or live-call verification. #1485 appears to have been swept into an unrelated batch closure rather than substantively resolved -- its own acceptance criterion (a live or explicit-dry-run `create_webhook_trigger` call) was never actually satisfied. This record exists so the gap is not lost a second time to the same failure mode; whoever picks this up should close it only against real evidence of a live (or explicit dry-run) call, not a batch commit that doesn't mention the file.

## Deliverables

- Re-run `ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` in a session where the tool may be reachable -- 4 consecutive interactive-session misses is a strong signal worth testing in a different session type (cloud/routine) if one becomes available.
- Once reachable, call `create_webhook_trigger` against a real (or an explicit, logged dry-run) routine and record its actual required fields, response shape, and any App-not-installed error text.
- Diff the actual response against what `plugin/skills/routine/webhook-trigger.md` currently documents (Step 5's assembled body, the `routine_trigger_id` field, the App-not-installed error detection) and correct any mismatch.
- Before closing, verify the closing commit/PR actually touches `webhook-trigger.md` or names the live-verification evidence directly -- do not let this close via an unrelated batch sweep the way #1485 did.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A live (or explicit dry-run) `create_webhook_trigger` call has been made and its actual request/response shape is confirmed to match (or has been corrected to match) `plugin/skills/routine/webhook-trigger.md`.
- The closing commit or PR description names this evidence directly (a transcript excerpt, a diff to `webhook-trigger.md`, or an explicit "confirmed matching, no changes needed" note) rather than a bare `Fixes #N` in an unrelated batch.

## Technical Approach

Start with `ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` in whichever session type is available at build time. If reachable, make one real or explicit-dry-run `create_webhook_trigger` call and capture its actual request/response shape verbatim before touching the docs. Then diff that captured shape against `webhook-trigger.md`'s current documentation section by section (assembled body, `routine_trigger_id`, App-not-installed error detection) and correct only what actually differs.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/routine/webhook-trigger.md` -- the documented request/response shape to verify and correct

## Gotchas

- If `RemoteTrigger`/`create_webhook_trigger` is still unreachable in whatever session builds this record, do not fabricate a "verified" result and do not close this record -- report the continued unavailability plainly (a 5th consecutive miss is itself a useful data point) and leave it open.
- Do not let this close via a bulk/batch commit that references this issue number without actually touching the files above -- that is exactly how #1485 was lost.

_Filed by `ledger resolve gate` via specShapedBody._
